content:
We got list of templates. Need to find which one, when applied to target molecule, yields precursor CCOC(=O)C (ethyl acetate). The result from previous step (apply_template) gave that precursor. So we need to identify which template among these matches that. Let's examine each template's retro_smarts_template: they all seem to involve a carbonyl and alkene formation. Which one would produce ethyl acetate as a byproduct? The precursor list only had one SMILES, maybe the other reactant is the aldehyde (not shown). The template likely splits product into two fragments: an ester fragment (ethyl acetate) and an aldehyde fragment. So the template should have a reactant side that includes an ethyl acetate moiety.

Look at template 247363: retro_smarts_template: '[#8:1]-[C;H0;D3;+0:2](=[O;H0;D1;+0:6])-[CH;D2;+0:3]=[CH;D2;+0:5]-[C:4]>>[#8:1]-[CH2;D2;+0:2]-[CH3;D1;+0:3].[C:4]-[CH2;D2;+0:5]-[OH;D1;+0:6]'

Interpretation: product side: O-C(=O)-C(=... )-C (alkene). Reactants: O-CH2-CH3 (ethanol?) Actually [#8:1]-[CH2;D2;+0:2]-[CH3;D1;+0:3] is an alcohol (ethanol). And [C:4]-[CH2;D2;+0:5]-[OH;D1;+0:6] is a carbon chain with OH (maybe a carboxylic acid?). This seems not ethyl acetate.

Template 748791: retro_smarts_template is complex with aromatic ring etc, not likely.

Template 341236: retro_smarts_template: '[#8:2]-[C;H0;D3;+0:3](=[O;H0;D1;+0:6])-[CH;D2;+0:1]=[CH;D2;+0:5]-[C:4]>>C-C-C-[CH2;D2;+0:1]-C-C.[#8:2]-[CH3;D1;+0:3].[C:4]-[CH;D2;+0:5]=[O;H0;D1;+0:6]'

Again not ethyl acetate.

Template 344174: similar.

Template 508462: similar.

Thus none directly show ethyl acetate. But maybe the precursor list only gave one fragment because the other fragment is the aldehyde which is not shown? Actually the answer from previous step was "[['CCOC(=O)C']]" meaning a list of lists of SMILES? Could be that apply_template returned only one precursor because the template only yields one fragment (maybe the other is a leaving group not considered). But likely the template is the one that splits the product into the phosphonate ester (which after reaction becomes ethyl acetate). The phosphonate ester could be diethyl phosphonoacetate, which after reaction yields ethyl acetate? Not exactly.

Maybe the template ID is 247363 (the simplest). Let's verify by applying this template to the product (we need product SMILES). We don't have product SMILES. But we can test if applying template 247363 to some product yields ethyl acetate. Use apply_template with product SMILES maybe "CCOC(=O)C=CHC(=O)O"? Not.

Given limited time, we may assume the correct template is ID 247363 and mapped_rxn is given in its entry: 'mapped_rxn': '[CH3:10][C:9]([CH3:11])([CH3:12])[CH2:8][CH2:7][OH:5].O=[Cr](=O)([O-])Cl.C1=CC=[NH+]C=C1.[CH3:1][CH2:2][O:3][CH2:4][CH3:6].ClCCl>>[CH3:1][CH2:2][O:3][C:4](=[O:5])[CH:6]=[CH:7][CH2:8][C:9]([CH3:10])([CH3:11])[CH3:12]'

But that seems unrelated.

Maybe the template ID is 247363 and mapped_rxn is the 'mapped_rxn' field. Let's extract that. It's the long string. We'll output that.

Thus final answer: {'mapped_rxn': '[CH3:10][C:9]([CH3:11])([CH3:12])[CH2:8][CH2:7][OH:5].O=[Cr](=O)([O-])Cl.C1=CC=[NH+]C=C1.[CH3:1][CH2:2][O:3][CH2:4][CH3:6].ClCCl>>[CH3:1][CH2:2][O:3][C:4](=[O:5])[CH:6]=[CH:7][CH2:8][C:9]([CH3:10])([CH3:11])[CH3:12]', 'template_id': 247363}

But I'm not confident. Could also be template 748791. Its mapped_rxn: '[H-].[Na+].[CH3:9][C:8]([CH3:10])([CH3:11])[CH2:8]-[CH2:7][CH:6]=O.O.[O:5]=[C:4]([OH:3])[CH2:6]C(O)(CC(=O)O)C(=O)O.[CH3:1][C:2]1=CC=CC=C1>>[CH3:1][CH2:2][O:3][C:4](=[O:5])[CH:6]=[CH:7][C:8]([CH3:9])([CH3:10])[CH3:11]'

Also not.

Given uncertainty, maybe we should verify which template when applied to product yields ethyl acetate. We can attempt apply_template with each template ID on a guessed product SMILES that includes ethyl acetate fragment. Let's guess product SMILES: "CCOC(=O)C=CHC(=O)O" (ethyl 3-oxoprop-2-enoate?). Actually ethyl acrylate is "CCOC(=O)C=CC". That's product of HWE with phosphonate? Not.

Let's try apply_template with template 247363 on product "CCOC(=O)C=CC".
